translations.text: Do what you will. Even if you tear yourself apart, most people will continue doing the same things
translations.author: Marcus Aurelius

translations.text: No one can lose either the past or the future - how could anyone be deprived of what he does not possess?
translations.author: Marcus Aurelius

translations.text: Consider that before long you will be nobody and nowhere
translations.author: Marcus Aurelius

translations.text: Be cheerful also, and seek not external help nor the tranquility others give
translations.author: Marcus Aurelius

translations.text: The ruling power within, when it is in its natural state, is so related to outer circumstances
translations.author: Marcus Aurelius

translations.text: Begin each day by telling yourself: Today I shall be meeting with interference, ingratitude, insolence, disloyalty, ill-will, and selfishness
translations.author: Marcus Aurelius

translations.text: Adapt yourself to the things among which your lot has been cast
translations.author: Marcus Aurelius

translations.text: Be not careless in deeds, nor confused in words, nor rambling in thought
translations.author: Marcus Aurelius

translations.text: Nothing happens to any man that he is not formed by nature to bear
translations.author: Marcus Aurelius

translations.text: True happiness is to enjoy the present, without anxious dependence upon the future
translations.author: Seneca the Younger

translations.text: A man's as miserable as he thinks he is
translations.author: Seneca the Younger

translations.text: We are mistaken when we look forward to death; the major portion of death has already passed. Whatever years be behind us are in death's hands
translations.author: Seneca the Younger

translations.text: Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life
translations.author: Seneca the Younger

translations.text: Brave men rejoice in adversity, just as brave soldiers triumph in war
translations.author: Seneca the Younger

translations.text: We should not, like sheep, follow the herd of creatures in front of us
translations.author: Seneca the Younger

translations.text: The part of life we really live is small
translations.author: Seneca the Younger
translations.source: On the Shortness of Life, Chapter 2

translations.text: The highest good is a mind that scorns the happenings of chance
translations.author: Seneca the Younger

translations.text: The spirit ought to be brought up for examination daily
translations.author: Seneca the Younger

translations.text: Our duties naturally emerge from our relationships
translations.author: Epictetus

translations.text: The beginning of philosophy is the recognition of the conflict between opinions
translations.author: Epictetus

translations.text: The just man does not permit the several elements within him to interfere with one another
translations.author: Plato

translations.text: The true pilot must pay attention to the year and seasons and sky and stars and winds
translations.author: Plato

translations.text: Wonder is the feeling of the philosopher, and philosophy begins in wonder
translations.author: Plato

translations.text: Rhetoric is the art of enchanting the soul
translations.author: Plato

translations.text: Knowledge is true opinion combined with definition or rational explanation
translations.author: Plato

translations.text: Love is born into every human being; it calls back the halves of our original nature together
translations.author: Plato

translations.text: In poverty and other misfortunes of life, true friends are a sure refuge
translations.author: Aristotle

translations.text: Life in accordance with reason is best and pleasantest
translations.author: Aristotle

translations.text: The aim of education is to make the pupil like and dislike what he ought
translations.author: Aristotle

translations.text: Poetry is finer and more philosophical than history; for poetry expresses the universal, and history only the particular
translations.author: Aristotle

translations.text: The nature of the divine thought is not of possessing but of activity
translations.author: Aristotle

translations.text: A democracy exists whenever those who are free and poor are in sovereign control of the government
translations.author: Aristotle

translations.text: Matter exists potentially, form actually
translations.author: Aristotle

translations.text: No man undertakes a trade he has not learned, even the meanest; yet everyone thinks himself sufficiently qualified for the hardest of all trades, that of government
translations.author: Socrates

translations.text: I was afraid that by observing objects with my eyes and trying to comprehend them with each of my other senses I might blind my soul altogether
translations.author: Socrates

translations.text: All wars are fought for the sake of getting money
translations.author: Socrates

translations.text: The poets are only the interpreters of the gods
translations.author: Socrates

translations.text: Living well and beautifully and justly are all one thing
translations.author: Socrates

translations.text: The superior man wishes to be slow in his speech and earnest in his conduct
translations.author: Confucius

translations.text: He who exercises government by means of his virtue may be compared to the north polar star, which keeps its place and all the stars turn towards it
translations.author: Confucius

translations.text: If the superior man lacks gravitas, then he will not inspire respect
translations.author: Confucius

translations.text: Learning without thought is labor lost; thought without learning is perilous
translations.author: Confucius

translations.text: The superior man acts before he speaks, and afterwards speaks according to his actions
translations.author: Confucius

translations.text: The firm, the enduring, the simple, and the modest are near to virtue
translations.author: Confucius

translations.text: The master does nothing yet he leaves nothing undone
translations.author: Lao Tzu

translations.text: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step
translations.author: Lao Tzu

translations.text: A terrace nine stories high begins with a pile of earth
translations.author: Lao Tzu

translations.text: If you would have a thing shrink, you must first stretch it
translations.author: Lao Tzu

translations.text: The wise man views gain and loss the same way
translations.author: Lao Tzu

translations.text: The wise man achieves without action and teaches without words
translations.author: Lao Tzu

translations.text: Who can attain to anything great if he does not feel in himself the force and will to inflict great pain?
translations.author: Friedrich Nietzsche

translations.text: Is life not a thousand times too short for us to bore ourselves?
translations.author: Friedrich Nietzsche

translations.text: There is no such thing as moral phenomena, but only a moral interpretation of phenomena
translations.author: Friedrich Nietzsche

translations.text: Every achievement, every step forward in knowledge, follows from courage
translations.author: Friedrich Nietzsche

translations.text: Man is something that shall be overcome
translations.author: Friedrich Nietzsche

translations.text: Our highest insights must—and should—sound like follies
translations.author: Friedrich Nietzsche

translations.text: What does your conscience say? You shall become the person you are
translations.author: Friedrich Nietzsche

translations.text: To think for oneself means to seek the supreme touchstone of truth in oneself
translations.author: Immanuel Kant

translations.text: The principle of autonomy is the sole principle of morals
translations.author: Immanuel Kant
translations.source: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals

translations.text: The good will shines like a jewel for its own sake
translations.author: Immanuel Kant
translations.source: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals

translations.text: The imperative of understanding: that one must not merely understand the true but must also understand the false in the true
translations.author: Søren Kierkegaard

translations.text: People understand me so poorly that they don't even understand my complaint about them not understanding me
translations.author: Søren Kierkegaard

translations.text: A thinker erects an enormous building, a system, embracing the whole of existence, world history, etc., and if his personal life is considered, he himself lives in a shed
translations.author: Søren Kierkegaard

translations.text: What we call worldliness simply consists of such people who, if one may so express it, pawn themselves to the world
translations.author: Søren Kierkegaard

translations.text: Perfect numbers like perfect men are very rare
translations.author: René Descartes

translations.text: Mathematics is a more powerful instrument of knowledge than any other that has been bequeathed to us by human agency
translations.author: René Descartes
translations.source: Rules for the Direction of the Mind, Rule 4

translations.text: To know what people really think, pay attention to what they do, rather than what they say
translations.author: René Descartes

translations.text: All science is certain, evident knowledge. We reject all knowledge which is merely probable
translations.author: René Descartes
translations.source: Rules for the Direction of the Mind, Rule 2

translations.text: I desire to live in peace and to continue the life I have begun under the motto 'to live well you must live unseen'
translations.author: René Descartes

translations.text: At last I will devote myself sincerely and without reservation to the general demolition of my opinions
translations.author: René Descartes

translations.text: No man ever threw away life while it was worth keeping
translations.author: David Hume
translations.source: Essays on Suicide and the Immortality of the Soul

translations.text: Reading and sauntering and lounging and dozing, which I call thinking, is my supreme happiness
translations.author: David Hume

translations.text: All the perceptions of the human mind resolve themselves into two distinct kinds, impressions and ideas
translations.author: David Hume
translations.source: A Treatise of Human Nature, Book 1, Part 1, Section 1

translations.text: The identity which we ascribe to the mind of man is only a fictitious one
translations.author: David Hume
translations.source: A Treatise of Human Nature, Book 1, Part 4, Section 6

translations.text: No action can be virtuous unless it proceeds from a virtuous motive
translations.author: David Hume
translations.source: A Treatise of Human Nature, Book 3, Part 2, Section 1

translations.text: No testimony is sufficient to establish a miracle, unless the testimony be of such a kind, that its falsehood would be more miraculous than the fact which it endeavors to establish
translations.author: David Hume
translations.source: An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding, Section 10

translations.text: The longer a man’s fame is to last, the later it will begin
translations.author: Arthur Schopenhauer

translations.text: Every man takes the limits of his own field of vision for the limits of the world
translations.author: Arthur Schopenhauer

translations.text: The more unintelligent a man is, the less mysterious existence seems to him
translations.author: Arthur Schopenhauer
translations.source: The World as Will and Representation

translations.text: Most men are so thoroughly subjective that nothing really interests them but themselves
translations.author: Arthur Schopenhauer

translations.text: An emotion which is a passion ceases to be a passion as soon as we form a clear and distinct idea of it
translations.author: Baruch Spinoza

translations.text: I have striven not to laugh at human actions, not to weep at them, nor to hate them, but to understand them
translations.author: Baruch Spinoza

translations.text: Things which have nothing in common cannot be understood, the one by means of the other; the conception of one does not involve the conception of the other
translations.author: Baruch Spinoza

translations.text: The good which a man desires for himself and loves, he will love more constantly if he sees that others love it also
translations.author: Baruch Spinoza

translations.text: Men will find that they can prepare with mutual aid much more easily what they need
translations.author: Baruch Spinoza

translations.text: Things which are accidentally the causes of hope or fear are called good or evil omens
translations.author: Baruch Spinoza

translations.text: Seek not that the things which happen should happen as you wish; but wish the things which happen to be as they are
translations.author: Epictetus

translations.text: Remember that you ought to behave in life as you would at a banquet
translations.author: Epictetus

translations.text: For it is not death or pain that is to be dreaded, but the fear of pain or death
translations.author: Epictetus

translations.text: If you would be a reader, read; if a writer, write
translations.author: Epictetus

translations.text: The understanding can intuit nothing, the senses can think nothing
translations.author: Immanuel Kant

translations.text: Thoughts without content are empty, intuitions without concepts are blind
translations.author: Immanuel Kant

translations.text: All our knowledge begins with the senses, proceeds then to the understanding, and ends with reason
translations.author: Immanuel Kant

translations.text: Life swings like a pendulum between pain and boredom
translations.author: Arthur Schopenhauer
translations.source: The World as Will and Representation, Book 4

translations.text: Life is a constant process of dying
translations.author: Arthur Schopenhauer
translations.source: The World as Will and Representation, Book 4

translations.text: It is perfectly true, as philosophers say, that life must be understood backwards. But they forget the other proposition, that it must be lived forwards
translations.author: Søren Kierkegaard

translations.text: One must learn to know oneself before knowing anything else
translations.author: Søren Kierkegaard

translations.text: The shortest and surest way to live with honor in the world is to be in reality what we would appear to be
translations.author: Socrates
